title: Day 10 — The Accidental O(n·m) Join
prompt: This nightly job attaches customer names to orders. It's fine in staging but takes minutes in prod and we miss the export window. Take a look — how would you speed it up?

clarifications.answer: Output must be identical — same fields, same order as the input orders. Only the performance should change.
If two customers share an id, the FIRST one in the list wins. Watch out — a naive dict comprehension keeps the last.
An order with no matching customer gets customer_name = None.
It's currently O(n*m) — a scan over all customers for every order. Target O(n+m).
Extra memory for an index is fine; O(m) for the lookup table is expected.
No need to sort — a hash lookup is O(1) average, better than sorting for this.

hints: What is the cost of the inner 'for c in customers' loop, and how many times does it run?
It's a nested-loop join: O(orders × customers). Replace the inner scan with a dict lookup keyed by customer id.
Build the index with setdefault so the FIRST customer for a given id wins (a dict comprehension would keep the last), then map each order through it.
